name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Father is Sudanese by birth at the time of the applicant's birth, OR (since the 2006 amendment) mother is Sudanese by birth -- the applicant may apply for recognition on this basis.

requirement_groups.name: Pre-1956 ancestral residence (historical, largely closed to new applicants)

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant and their paternal ancestors were residing in Sudan continuously since 1 January 1956 (Sudan's independence date) -- given the 70+ years elapsed, this specific retroactive provision is now relevant mainly to establishing an existing claim rather than a genuinely new application route.

evidence_required.document: Parent's proof of Sudanese citizenship by birth

sources.title: Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative -- Sudanese Nationality Act 1994, as amended: original text ties birthright citizenship to a Sudanese-by-birth FATHER; the 2006 amendment adds that a person 'born to a mother who is Sudanese by birth shall be entitled to Sudanese Nationality by birth whenever he applies for it'; a separate retroactive provision covers persons (and their paternal ancestors) 'residing in Sudan since 1/1/1956'; children of unknown parents found in Sudan are presumed Sudanese nationals

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sudan). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2-only sourcing limitation as the other Sudan citizenship files. GENDERED HISTORY, DISCLOSED PRECISELY: descent citizenship was PATERNAL-ONLY from the Act's 1994 enactment until a 2006 amendment introduced maternal transmission -- and even the 2006 text frames maternal transmission as something the applicant 'shall be entitled to... whenever he applies for it' (an application-triggered entitlement) rather than automatic-by-birth the way paternal transmission is framed, a phrasing difference worth flagging as a possible remaining procedural asymmetry even after the reform, though not confirmed as a hard practical difference in this build. The 2018 amendment's separate 'domicile since 1 January 1924' provision (mentioned in the source only in connection with exemptions from the automatic-revocation-on-acquiring-South-Sudanese-citizenship rule -- see sd_citizenship_naturalisation.json) is NOT modeled here since it functions as a revocation exemption, not an acquisition route. dual_citizenship_allowed FALSE, consistent with the other Sudan citizenship files.
